# PR-head review threads: acme/widget#82 (N=1)

## Setup

**Aliases**

| Alias | Value |
|---|---|
| ROOT | `/work/widget` |
| W | `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` |
| H | `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` (headRefOid, `aaaaaaa`) |
| B | `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` (origin/main, `bbbbbbb`) |

Provisioning and the base merge are complete. W is clean on `fix/retry` at H, and the base merge was a no-op. Both H and B are proven ancestors of HEAD. The process cwd stays ROOT, and no `cd` is run.

**Query owner:** `reference/pr-head.md`, section "Fetch unresolved review threads". It owns two queries, which this narration cites rather than copies:
- **Q1:** the reviewThreads query.
- **Q2:** the per-thread comment follow-up query.

The fetch runs once per admitted PR, so it runs for this N=1 run, before gather.

## Command legend

| # | cwd | Command |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | ROOT | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query='<Q1>' -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` |
| C2 | ROOT | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query='<Q2>' -F id=<T1 id>` |

## Successful fetch

**C1** follows the reviewThreads cursor across three pages, and I merge the pages:

| Page | Thread | isResolved | Kept? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T1 | false | yes |
| 2 | T2 (outdated) | false | yes |
| 2 | TX | true | **filtered out** |
| 3 | T3 | false | yes |

**T1 comment pagination**
- T1 reports `comments.pageInfo.hasNextPage=true` and `totalCount=102`, which is more than the first page holds.
- I run **C2** for T1 with its own comment cursor, separate from the reviewThreads cursor. It starts at T1's first comment page and fetches until `hasNextPage=false`.
- C2 returns 102 comments across two pages:
  - Page 1 has 100 comments: the first comment plus replies 1–99.
  - Page 2 has replies 100–101.
- I replace T1's initial 100 comments with C2's complete connection, so no comment is duplicated.

T2 and T3 report no further comment pages, so they need no follow-up.

**Every comment carries the same supplied metadata:**
- url: `https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1`
- author: `reviewer`
- createdAt: `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`

**Location rule:** `<path>:<line>`; else `<path>:<originalLine> (outdated)`; else `<path>`.

### Rendered threads (comments in order)

**T1 — `src/retry.ts:12`**

| # | Body |
|---|---|
| 1 | Rewrite the retry engine |
| 2–101 (replies 1–100) | Rewrite still requested |
| 102 (reply 101) | Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines. |

The effective request comes from reading every reply, not just the first comment:
- The first comment asks to rewrite the engine.
- The last reply, on comment page 2 and only reached through C2, overrides that.
- **Repair request: keep the retry engine; cap retries in two lines.**
- The rewrite request is superseded and is not carried forward as the ask.

**T2 — `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)`** (line=null, originalLine=7)

| # | Body |
|---|---|
| 1 | Keep this guard |
| 2 | Yes, retain it |

**Request:** retain the guard in `src/old.ts`. No code change is asked for.

**T3 — `README.md`** (line=null, originalLine=null)

| # | Body |
|---|---|
| 1 | Document the cap |

**Request:** document the retry cap in README.

**Thread record for #82:** 3 unresolved threads (T1, T2, T3), carried to gather. TX is excluded because it is resolved.

## Failed fetch (independent case)

C1, or C2 for any thread, returns `API unavailable`.

**Stop, before gather and before the spec:**

```text
threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)
```

- This stop applies to this N=1 run as well.
- No partial thread set is used.
- No spec is drafted, no Rework record is written, and no `Threads: none` record is written.
- Nothing is pushed.
- W stays as provisioned: clean on `fix/retry` at H.

## Empty set (independent case)

C1 succeeds, but no thread has `isResolved == false`. Either there are zero threads, or all are resolved, as TX is. No C2 runs.

**Record:**

```text
Threads: none
```

The flow then continues to gather for #82.

I’m using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace. As requested, this narration covers only review-thread fetching after successful provisioning.

### Setup and command legend

- `ROOT=/work/widget`; `W=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.
- PR: `acme/widget#82`; singleton run, `N=1`.
- **Query/pagination owner:** `using-git-worktrees/reference/pr-head.md`, “Fetch unresolved review threads.”
- `QT` denotes that owner’s exact reviewThreads query; `QC` denotes its exact thread-comments query. These are notation aliases, not additional commands.
- Every command below runs with **cwd=`W`**. `--paginate` follows the relevant connection through its final page. Review-thread and comment cursors remain separate.

The successful, failed, and empty fetches below are independent alternatives, not successive mutations. No provisioning, base-merge, or Step 4 commands/report are repeated.

### Successful fetch

| Order | Command, exact arguments using query aliases | Result/action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | Fetch all three reviewThreads pages and combine them in page order. T1 requires comment pagination: `totalCount=102`, first-page `hasNextPage=true`. |
| 2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QC" -F id=T1` | Start at T1’s **first comment page**, using its own cursor; fetch through the last page. Replace T1’s initial comments with this complete connection—do not append duplicate first-page comments. |

Filter the combined threads to `isResolved == false`: retain T1, T2, T3; exclude resolved TX.

**Shared metadata `M`, attached to every individual comment below:**

```text
url: https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1
author: reviewer
createdAt: 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z
```

The indexed range below represents each comment individually, in ascending order, with metadata `M`; it does not collapse or discard replies.

| Thread/location | Complete ordered comments |
|---|---|
| **T1 — `src/retry.ts:12`** | Comment 1: “Rewrite the retry engine” — M. Comments 2–101, respectively replies 1–100: each “Rewrite still requested” — M each. Comment 102, reply 101: “Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines.” — M. |
| **T2 — `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)`** | Comment 1: “Keep this guard” — M. Comment 2: “Yes, retain it” — M. |
| **T3 — `README.md`** | Comment 1: “Document the cap” — M. |

**Carried repair requests:**
- **T1:** The final reply changes the request: **keep the engine; cap retries in two lines**, rather than rewrite it.
- **T2:** Retain the guard, including the confirming reply and outdated location.
- **T3:** Document the cap.

All comments remain available in order for gather; the final T1 reply is not lost to first-page truncation.

### Independent failed fetch

| Order | Command, cwd=`W` | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | Error: `API unavailable` |

**Stop:** `threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)`

This singleton run stops **before gather and spec**. No comment follow-up, draft, or continuation record is produced.

### Independent successful empty fetch

| Order | Command, cwd=`W` | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | Successful fetch; no unresolved threads remain. |

Record: **`Threads: none`**. No comment-pagination command is needed.
